nodes.label: Transcription & translation engine (dual-stream)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Non-Latin spoken audio needs a phonetic/Roman transliteration stream alongside a timestamp-aligned English translation, both through provider-agnostic BYOK endpoints.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/relay/process pipeline (8 steps)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Download and audio-extract via Bun $, decrypt the provider key, transcribe plus timestamped translation, route to a selected or synthesized agent schema, enforce evidence citation, render and publish through the Ray, then delete temp media.

nodes.label: 0.2.0 - Credentials Dashboard & Notion Ray
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown

nodes.label: Task 4.4-4.6: Extraction, Grounding & Notion Publishing
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Per-property evidence citations were replaced with transcript-and-caption grounding scored on content-word overlap and flagged, never silently dropped; no model id or prompt is hardcoded.

nodes.label: PRD strict out of scope (MVP)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Excludes paid scraping APIs, frame-by-frame OCR/CV, multi-tenant billing and permanent cloud media storage to keep the MVP self-hosted and private.

nodes.label: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.norm_label: relay (prd): short-form video to evidence-grounded markdown
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted and BYOK because users should not pay SaaS markup for scrapers or LLM wrappers, and local extraction keeps media and tokens private.

nodes.label: Document tree and Notion publish (Task 4.6)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: render/document.ts builds a TREE, never a Markdown string, because a string would force every future destination to re-parse structure it already had; notion-blocks.ts is the only Notion-aware file so a second Ray adds a sibling. Evidence becomes a toggle containing a quote with the timestamp in the summary, and the parent page is DISCOVERED rather than configured because an integration only sees what was shared with it.

nodes.label: The evidence contract is structural, not requested
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.norm_label: the evidence contract is structural, not requested
nodes.rationale: Agent schemas embed a oneOf of transcript and visual evidence shapes discriminated by kind, so the vision tier adds a producer and a verifier branch rather than a migration. The synthesizer never writes JSON Schema itself -- it proposes a field plan and compile() injects evidence on every field, because a model asked for JSON Schema will eventually emit one where evidence is optional and that schema would be persisted and reused.

nodes.label: Evidence verification (Task 4.5)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Two checks per claim: the quote must appear in the normalised English transcript AND the cited ms range must overlap the segments it was found in. The bar is an exact normalised substring with no fuzzy threshold, because a similarity cutoff would let a paraphrase through -- the one thing the feature exists to prevent; tokenOverlap only labels failures QUOTE_ALTERED vs QUOTE_NOT_FOUND. Normalisation is lossy in form only. Findings are flagged, not dropped.

nodes.label: Planned Task 4.3b: frame/vision extraction (amends PRD §5)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Most Reels/Shorts are music over on-screen text with no speech and empty descriptions, so frames are the only content source and the PRD's out-of-scope CV line is amended. Frame-derived fields carry visual evidence explicitly marked as a weaker claim than a verbatim quote; Groq has no vision models so Gemini's free tier is the intended provider.

nodes.label: Groq free-tier TPM pressure and mitigations
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.norm_label: groq free-tier tpm pressure and mitigations
nodes.rationale: 8000 TPM with the transcript crossing the wire twice per run means back-to-back runs 429, so routing sees a 4000-char truncation (it only needs the clip's kind) and runChat waits out the provider's advised delay once; under sustained pressure the router still degrades to weaker models that fail schema validation.

nodes.label: Media ingest gotchas (ffmpeg exit 8, Bun $ newline, rm no-op)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.norm_label: media ingest gotchas (ffmpeg exit 8, bun $ newline, rm no-op)
nodes.rationale: Three silent failures: ffmpeg exits 8 on --version so version flags are per-binary; a newline inside a Bun $ template is a command separator, so invocations are single-line with argv arrays; Bun's rm builtin silently no-ops on Windows for ./ paths, so every run leaked media and purge() now verifies the directory is gone instead of trusting the exit code.

nodes.label: OpenRouter is 6-15x slower than Groq
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Measured extraction 74s/35s/88s versus ~5s on Groq, and one run took 303.5s against the PRD's sub-30s whole-pipeline target, so moving Groq ahead of OpenRouter in EXTRACTION_ORDER is a one-line change and strongly indicated.

nodes.label: Transcription gotchas (Whisper fabrication, no_speech_prob gate)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Whisper fabricates speech on music-only audio, which would feed invented content to extraction -- the exact failure the product exists to prevent -- so output is gated on no_speech_prob and discarded text is retained for auditing. avg_logprob is anti-correlated and unusable. A decoding prompt to force Latin script did not work and contaminated output. Transliteration is line-by-line with a segment-count check so timestamps stay aligned, and hasSpeech:false is a signal, not a throw.

nodes.label: Evidence grounding / hallucination risk
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Generative extraction invents steps, metrics and ingredients, so every property carries timestamp_start, timestamp_end and transcript_quote; the success metric is 100% grounding.

nodes.label: Bun-first mandate (Bun-native and Web-standard APIs)
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: Bun runs everything and Next starts via bun --bun so Bun-native APIs work at runtime: WebCrypto over node:crypto, Uint8Array hex/base64 over Buffer, Bun.$ over child_process; a node:* import is allowed only where Bun ships no equivalent, e.g. node:stream for pino.

nodes.label: Fixed-viewport dashboard shell
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.rationale: The (dashboard) shell never scrolls (h-svh overflow-hidden on SidebarInset) and only ShellContent's ScrollArea does; overflow must not be set globally on html/body because setting overflow-y on both disables html->body scroll propagation and public pages get a double scrollbar.

nodes.label: Layout must not dance while loading
nodes.community_name: Relay (PRD): short-form video to evidence-grounded Markdown
nodes.norm_label: layout must not dance while loading
nodes.rationale: A skeleton mirrors the real component and reserves every element's height so nothing moves between loading and loaded; client-only values render a same-sized placeholder.

nodes.label: Queue admission control (src/lib/queue/admission.ts)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Three locks, none of which can FAIL a run: over budget is a later, not a never, so the job is delayed and relay_runs keeps the row at queued.

nodes.label: Branch A: yt-dlp-only consolidation
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Deletes instaloader.ts and its binary spec, drops python3/pip and INSTALOADER_* from the Dockerfile, and restores the deliberately Python-free slim base; the sources[] machinery is kept because it is correct and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Branch B: instaloader stays, session derived per run
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: branch b: instaloader stays, session derived per run
nodes.rationale: instaloader consumes its own pickled session keyed to a username, so Netscape stays canonical and a tiny adapter materializes instaloader's form inside the run's temp dir and dies with it -- one canonical secret, one derived artifact.

nodes.label: capture session (headful Chromium + Xvfb instance)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources

nodes.label: jar (Netscape-format cookie file)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Netscape is the interchange format because it is what CDP Storage.getCookies maps onto cleanly and what yt-dlp --cookies consumes; storing two formats would double the secret surface and let them drift.

nodes.label: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: session_auth: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Not 'unblock Instagram' and not 'unblock YouTube': it gives every source an optional per-user signed-in session so a rate-limited source degrades to 'reconnect your account' instead of a dead end. Capture is insurance against a currently dormant failure mode, which is why the cheap deterministic fixes are sequenced first.

nodes.label: Capture security model (loopback CDP, ticket, fenced navigation)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: capture security model (loopback cdp, ticket, fenced navigation)
nodes.rationale: The CDP port is unauthenticated so it is loopback-only on an ephemeral port; socket auth is Origin + single-use atomic GETDEL ticket + session ownership re-checked per message; navigation is fenced to the provider's domains because otherwise an authenticated user could steer a server-side browser into the VPS's private network (SSRF with a keyboard); frames are Zod-validated and malformed ones dropped silently because an echo is an oracle; the browser is spawned with a stripped env so VAULT_KEY never enters a process rendering third-party pages.

nodes.label: Deferral via moveToDelayed + DelayedError
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: The worker holds a job lock while processing, so moveToDelayed needs the token to release it and DelayedError stops BullMQ completing or failing the job; a deferral does not consume an attempt (verified). A user_busy deferral re-polls every 2s per queued run, which is the first cost to revisit if the queue gets deep.

nodes.label: Deferred: social cookie credentials (2026-08-31 decision)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Capture is a server-side browser the user drives, not a paste box or child window: window.open is cross-origin, document.cookie is origin-scoped and Instagram's sessionid is HttpOnly, so every workable route goes through a privileged context. Headful+Xvfb over --headless=new because Instagram fingerprints headless. Bonus: a cookie minted from the server's IP is reused from that IP, avoiding the mismatch that flags pasted cookies.

nodes.label: Per-user slot semaphore (fairness)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: config.queue.concurrency is one global number, so one user submitting 20 URLs occupied every slot; BullMQ OSS has no job groups and its limiter is global, so fairness is a Dragonfly semaphore across perUserConcurrency slots with a PX TTL as the crash net.

nodes.label: Per-credential rate budget as a rolling window
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: per-credential rate budget as a rolling window
nodes.rationale: Keyed on the credential because the account is what gets flagged; an exact ZSET rolling window rather than a fixed bucket, since a fixed hour lets a user spend the whole budget at :59 and the next at :00, and it makes 'when does room appear' exact. Both windows are checked before either is charged.

nodes.label: Zod validates all external input at the API boundary
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: zod validates all external input at the api boundary
nodes.rationale: Request bodies, query params and Ray callbacks are validated before touching the database or vault; shared schemas live in src/lib/schemas.ts.

nodes.label: §5.1 Capture concurrency cap and teardown
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: On a 4GB VPS two 500MB sessions leave headroom for a download+ffmpeg burst; 3 would fit on paper and lose it. The idle timer is the real reclaimer, not the TTL. Deliberately no wait-queue (MVP-first): a queue for a 2-slot once-per-user resource is machinery without a customer and a spinner that might resolve in 10 minutes is worse than an honest 503. Seven teardown paths exist because a leaked Chromium is 500MB that never comes back.

nodes.label: §1.2 Instagram consolidation hypothesis (blocked on proof)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: If yt-dlp --cookies works with a real signed-in jar, both sources collapse onto one downloader and Python leaves the image. 'Cookies are required' is proven (the extractor names --cookies itself); 'cookies are sufficient' is not (open issues report empty media responses). Experiment (c) decides it: if yt-dlp's extractor returns a null or junk title, agent routing silently degrades on every Reel -- plausible wrong output rather than an error, the worst failure mode in this codebase.

nodes.label: §5.5 No fixed frame rate, ack backpressure instead
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: §5.5 no fixed frame rate, ack backpressure instead
nodes.rationale: screencastFrameAck requests the next frame only after the client acknowledges the last, so the stream self-throttles to the slowest link instead of guessing an fps.

nodes.label: A third provider list is required (gap in the deferred note)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: a third provider list is required (gap in the deferred note)
nodes.rationale: credentialInputSchema.provider is z.enum(PROVIDER_IDS) derived from ALL_PROVIDERS, which contains neither instagram nor youtube, so a cookie credential would be rejected at the schema boundary today -- the claim that only the Drizzle enum and Zod schema were needed was incomplete.

nodes.label: §6 Risks (datacenter IP fingerprinting, password transit, jar blast radius)
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: §6 risks (datacenter ip fingerprinting, password transit, jar blast radius)
nodes.rationale: CDP attachment is itself a detection vector and is unmitigated by design choice, so it must be measured in Phase 2 rather than argued. The user's password transits the capture process's memory keystroke-by-keystroke and cannot be engineered away (sessionid is HttpOnly), so it must be stated in the Connect dialog. A jar is a bearer credential for a whole account, so disconnecting in Relay does not log the session out on the platform.

nodes.label: §5.6 What breaks first at 10 / 100 / 1000 users
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: At 10 users the pinch is throughput, not memory. At 100 it is the shared egress IP well before RAM, because a per-credential budget protects an account from its own burst, not from its neighbours. At 1000 the single VPS goes and per-user fairness must move from a Dragonfly semaphore to real queue partitioning.

nodes.label: §5.2 The screencast WebSocket is a remote-control channel
nodes.community_name: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.norm_label: §5.2 the screencast websocket is a remote-control channel
nodes.rationale: Browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket constructor, so a single-use 60s query-string ticket is the correct shape; reusing the app session cookie would make the socket CSRF-reachable from any origin. Redemption is atomic GETDEL, ownership is re-checked, Origin is checked, frames are Zod-validated, navigation is fenced (otherwise it is an SSRF-shaped proxy with a keyboard attached), and no frame or key event is ever logged.

nodes.label: Typography & iconography (Oxanium, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono, HugeIcons)
nodes.norm_label: typography & iconography (oxanium, space grotesk, jetbrains mono, hugeicons)

nodes.label: Component strictness: zero native form elements
nodes.norm_label: component strictness: zero native form elements
nodes.rationale: Native input/select/textarea/button are forbidden so every surface inherits the design system's states and accessibility wiring from ShadCN primitives.

nodes.label: GSAP animation standards (useGSAP, guarded refs)
nodes.rationale: GSAP is authorized only for micro-interactions, page transitions and pipeline progress; refs are guarded against App Router hydration mismatches and ordinary hover/focus stays on Tailwind transitions.

nodes.label: Relay UI/UX philosophy (data-dense command center)
nodes.rationale: Built for power users: Notion-like functional aesthetic, high-contrast dark default, compact density, collapsible sidebar plus expansive workbench.

nodes.label: Authenticated browser verification via signed auth_sessions cookie
nodes.norm_label: authenticated browser verification via signed auth_sessions cookie
nodes.rationale: agent-browser could not authenticate until a session row was minted and the cookie signed with better-auth's own makeSignature; the raw token is rejected because the cookie is token.hmac. It caught a dnd-kit hydration mismatch and a 380px truncation.

nodes.label: Explicit Clone replaces copy-on-write for System agents
nodes.norm_label: explicit clone replaces copy-on-write for system agents
nodes.rationale: A System agent is never edited or forked silently; one row button opens read-only View/Clone or editable Edit/Clone, and Clone switches mode in place with a non-colliding name. Row actions render uniform slots because hiding Delete left ragged rows that read as a rendering failure.

nodes.label: hover:scale replaced by hover:-translate-y-px
nodes.rationale: Scaling promotes an element to a composited layer and re-rasterises its text, which was the reported blur-on-hover; backdrop-blur was removed at the same time and the toast viewport moved to z-100 because at z-50 a later-mounted modal painted over it.

nodes.label: Modal shell over DialogContent (src/components/modal.tsx)
nodes.rationale: A three-row grid with static header/footer and a ScrollArea body, built because the agent editor's JSON Schema pushed Save off-screen; built over DialogContent because a hand-rolled portal looked identical but Base UI wires Escape, backdrop dismissal, focus trapping and DialogClose to its own Popup.

nodes.label: SESSION_EXPIRED classification (Phase 4)
nodes.rationale: A dead jar used to fail as SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, sending users to investigate a healthy video. Now a login-shaped failure with a jar supplied is SESSION_EXPIRED, permanent so BullMQ does not burn the attempt budget, with a message that never carries stderr because lastLine() puts 400 chars of raw stderr into the user-visible run.error. The CLIENT_REFUSED 403 branch runs first because a 403 means the same thing with or without a jar.

nodes.label: Brand logo linking rule
nodes.rationale: Always the PNG from config.assets.logo; public pages link to /, the dashboard shell links to /runs so a signed-in user clicking the logo is never bounced to the marketing page.

nodes.label: Light mode and mobile are first-class
nodes.norm_label: light mode and mobile are first-class
nodes.rationale: Tailwind -300/-200 shades read on near-black but wash out on white, so they need a paired darker light-mode shade; data-active/data-state primitives bake their own variants so an outside utility class loses on specificity and the override must use the matching data-attribute prefix. Verify both themes and ~390x844 with agent-browser.

nodes.label: Row-scoped actions rule
nodes.rationale: Operations on an existing record (reconnect, delete) live in that record's row; the page header holds only creation actions.

nodes.label: Solid colors only, no glass
nodes.rationale: No translucent tints, blurred glow shadows or backdrop-blur; accents use a solid fill instead of an opacity fraction over the background.

nodes.label: UI rule: ShadCN components and HugeIcons only
nodes.norm_label: ui rule: shadcn components and hugeicons only
nodes.rationale: No native form elements and no Lucide; every page build runs through the design-taste-frontend, gpt-taste, ui-styling and ui-ux-pro-max skills to avoid templated AI-slop layouts.

nodes.label: Vivid UI and living-app motion
nodes.rationale: No dead surfaces: each control gets its own hover accent plus motion feedback, and app-level state changes use the View Transitions API so a big change feels physical, always gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: §4.3 SESSION_EXPIRED rule (hinges on one bit of state)
nodes.norm_label: §4.3 session_expired rule (hinges on one bit of state)
nodes.rationale: If a jar was supplied and the failure is login-shaped it is not SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; the old message even advised signing in, useless advice to a user who already has. It is permanent, never carries stderr, and trips Reconnect only at two rejects because a single transient checkpoint should not nag a user whose session is fine.

nodes.label: OpenObserve observability (client RUM + server logs)
nodes.rationale: Hono HTTP logs, SQLite query errors and yt-dlp/ffmpeg stderr are routed to OpenObserve ingest streams alongside client RUM.

nodes.label: compose: capture service (Chromium, shm, seccomp)
nodes.rationale: Its own service because Next.js cannot upgrade a WebSocket and the cap needs one owner process; shm_size 1gb because Docker's 64MB /dev/shm crashes tabs; seccomp:unconfined with cap_drop ALL so Chromium can apply its own tighter per-renderer filter instead of running --no-sandbox; only /stream should ever be routed publicly; relay_data is deliberately not mounted.

nodes.label: compose: dragonfly service (pinned, allow-undeclared-keys)
nodes.rationale: --default_lua_flags=allow-undeclared-keys is required because BullMQ's Lua builds key names at runtime; pinned rather than :latest because Coolify pulls on every deploy, so a floating tag can change the queue backend under an app-only deploy.

nodes.label: compose: relay service (target runtime)
nodes.rationale: target: runtime is explicit and load-bearing -- with no target Docker builds the LAST stage (capture), so the web app silently shipped Chromium and ran as the capture user.

nodes.label: compose: worker service (init, health, cache-hit args)
nodes.norm_label: compose: worker service (init, health, cache-hit args)
nodes.rationale: Runs the pipeline out of band so a download never occupies a request handler; init:true because Bun as PID 1 does not reap yt-dlp/ffmpeg/instaloader grandchildren; the NEXT_PUBLIC args are repeated to keep the build a cache hit; depends_on relay is a migration ordering constraint, not a runtime one.

nodes.label: Authentication & Observability (Better Auth, Pino, Rays rebrand)
nodes.norm_label: authentication & observability (better auth, pino, rays rebrand)

nodes.label: Deployment: deps/builder/runtime Dockerfile stages
nodes.rationale: Build-only artefacts stay out of the shipped image and the base is pinned because the floating oven/bun:1 tag moved minors; the worker repeats the NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args because they bake into ENV and a mismatch cost 16.4s of duplicated compilation.

nodes.label: CAPTURE_INTERNAL_TOKEN (dedicated inter-service secret)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated secret with a `:?` guard so compose refuses to start without it; the config's VAULT_KEY fallback exists only for a zero-config dev box, and shipping it would send the master encryption key as an HTTP header between containers.

nodes.label: compose: json-file log rotation on every service
nodes.norm_label: compose: json-file log rotation on every service
nodes.rationale: Container logs are unbounded by default and the deploy target is a single VPS, while Coolify's cleanup prunes images rather than log files.

nodes.label: Better Auth drizzle adapter schema aliasing
nodes.norm_label: better auth drizzle adapter schema aliasing
nodes.rationale: The adapter's getSchema(model) is sometimes called with the base model name and sometimes the modelName override, so both must alias the same table or Google sign-in 500s with 'model auth_verifications was not found'.

nodes.label: Docker / Coolify deployment notes
nodes.rationale: Coolify rewrites every service image to <uuid>_<service>:<sha>, so relay and worker each build the Dockerfile instead of sharing a tag. Runtime contents are copied explicitly because one image runs three things needing different slices of the repo. Size barely moved because Bun hardlinks its install cache; a --production install is blocked because db:migrate shells out to drizzle-kit, a devDependency. init:true on the worker because Bun as PID 1 does not reap grandchildren.

nodes.label: Production outage: Dockerfile stage boundary
nodes.rationale: COPY/EXPOSE/CMD sat after FROM runtime AS capture, so they belonged to the capture stage: relay and worker (no target) built the LAST stage and shipped the 3.3GB Chromium image, while capture ran a second Next.js server that re-ran db:migrate concurrently and crash-looped until Coolify stopped the whole resource. Fixed by moving the block above the capture stage and pinning target: runtime.

nodes.label: BullMQ over Dragonfly queue architecture (Task 4.2)
nodes.rationale: POST /relay/process writes a queued row then enqueues and returns 202, so the request never waits on the pipeline and a job can never reference a missing row; relay_runs is the source of truth so a flushed Dragonfly loses scheduling, never history. --default_lua_flags=allow-undeclared-keys is MANDATORY because BullMQ's Lua builds key names at runtime; the {relay} hash tag is a throughput choice, not correctness.

nodes.label: Turso/libSQL adoption and non-automatic migrations
nodes.rationale: drizzle-orm/libsql replaced bun-sqlite. Auto-migrating on connection was removed because the sqlite migrator reads the last-applied row before opening its transaction, so parallel Next.js build workers could both decide a migration was pending and both apply it -- the root cause of the Coolify build failures.

nodes.label: Drizzle over libSQL driver with explicit migrations
nodes.norm_label: drizzle over libsql driver with explicit migrations
nodes.rationale: One client serves a local file: dev path and a remote Turso libsql:// URL. Migrations run only via the explicit db:migrate step because libsql's migrator is async while getDb() is synchronous, and auto-migrating per connection let concurrent Next.js build workers race on the same database.

nodes.label: Media source registry (src/lib/media/sources.ts)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Owns the supported-source vocabulary the way providers.ts owns credential providers: parseSourceUrl accepts only Reel and Shorts paths, normalises hosts and returns a tracking-free canonicalUrl, and SUPPORTED_SOURCE_LABELS derives all user copy so no pipeline code contains a source string literal.

nodes.label: §2.5 Capture routes (/capture/:provider, finish, cancel)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: A status poll route exists so the UI can recover if the WebSocket drops; the socket itself lives on the capture service, not in Next.js.

nodes.label: Source-scoped binary preflight (ensureMediaBinaries)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Every run checks its binaries before spawning and the error names the install command and override env var; only successful detections are cached so installing a binary on a running server takes effect without a restart, and the check is source-scoped so a YouTube-only operator is not blocked by instaloader.

nodes.label: Capture browser launch prerequisites (xauth, chromium-sandbox, seccomp)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.norm_label: capture browser launch prerequisites (xauth, chromium-sandbox, seccomp)
nodes.rationale: --no-install-recommends dropped xauth (xvfb-run shells out to it) and chromium-sandbox (Debian splits the setuid helper), and Docker's default seccomp denied clone(CLONE_NEWUSER). seccomp:unconfined with cap_drop ALL is the safer half of the trade because Chromium then applies its own tighter per-renderer filter instead of being run with --no-sandbox.

nodes.label: CAPTURE_PUBLIC_URL public wss route (open decision)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: ?? let an empty compose-expanded string through so the browser got a relative /stream that resolved to Next.js, which cannot upgrade; now ||. The service still has no public route, and a path-scoped Coolify domain would hit Caddy handle_path stripping the prefix and land on the token-gated control plane as a misleading 401.

nodes.label: Capture service as a third process (Phase 2)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.norm_label: capture service as a third process (phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Next.js route handlers cannot upgrade a request to a WebSocket (hono/vercel's handle() returns a Response), and the concurrency cap is only enforceable if exactly ONE process owns the map of live browsers, whereas Next.js runs several workers each with its own idea.

nodes.label: Three capture bugs found by testing
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.norm_label: three capture bugs found by testing
nodes.rationale: A relative --user-data-dir let Chrome fall back to the operator's real profile; ioredis lazy connect with enableOfflineQueue:false made the first redeemTicket after every deploy throw, so tickets use their own client with the offline queue on; a failed ticket orphaned a live browser holding ~400MB, so the route now tears the session down explicitly.

nodes.label: Instagram unblocked via instaloader
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: yt-dlp cannot fetch Reels anonymously but instaloader can. Five zero-dependency anonymous routes were tested from Bun fetch and all failed, so the cost is Python in a deliberately Python-free image. instaloader.ts maps Instagram's post JSON onto the same source_info shape as yt-dlp and synthesizes a title from the caption's first line, because Instagram has no title field and routing reads the title.

nodes.label: Three-tier link icon resolution
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Media-source brand mark, then bundled brand mark, then a favicon service, then a generic glyph; only the third tier touches the network and it is the browser calling out, so setting FAVICON_SERVICE_URL empty disables it.

nodes.label: Worker liveness endpoint (src/lib/queue/health.ts)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: A loopback Bun.serve reporting worker.isRunning(), because Docker and Coolify can otherwise only see that the process exists, which stays true after BullMQ stops consuming.

nodes.label: Config single source (README)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Every env var is read in src/config/index.ts and consumed as an import, so process.env is never read elsewhere and nothing is hardcoded.

nodes.label: Configuration mandate: src/config/index.ts only
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: App identity, server, API version, database URL, vault key, asset paths, theme and observability all flow through one exported config object; process.env is never read anywhere else.

nodes.label: No hardcoding rule
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Provider ids/labels live only in src/lib/providers.ts and env-derived values only in src/config, with types derived from that single source; MVP-first means minimal entries but scalable machinery.

nodes.label: Rays are provider-generic (registry, generic account_* keys)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.norm_label: rays are provider-generic (registry, generic account_* keys)
nodes.rationale: Flows go through src/server/ray-providers.ts with no provider-specific routes, cookies or strings in flow logic; registry entries map provider vocabulary onto generic account_id/name/email/avatar keys so vault, routes and UI consume only generic keys.

nodes.label: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.norm_label: §2.1 capture runs in its own bun process
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router handlers cannot upgrade to WebSocket (hono/vercel's handle() returns a Response) and a live Chromium handle is long-lived state a request-scoped handler cannot own; it also makes the concurrency cap enforceable because an in-memory session Map is only authoritative if one process owns it.

nodes.label: §2.4 CaptureProvider registry (provider-generic)
nodes.community_name: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: The exact analogue of ray-providers.ts, with loginUrl, sessionCookies, cookieDomains and a mapAccount that must return generic account_* keys. The social vocabulary derives from MEDIA_SOURCES rather than a hand-written second list, so a social credential's provider IS the media source id and download-time lookup needs no mapping table.

nodes.label: BYOK encrypted credential vault
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: Bring-Your-Own-Key avoids SaaS markup and keeps provider tokens under the user's control, AES-256-GCM at rest with zero plaintext exposure.

nodes.label: social credential (credentials row, type: cookie)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)

nodes.label: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: §3 storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: The whole Netscape jar is one AES-256-GCM encrypted string in access_token because the vault already treats it as an opaque secret, so no new crypto is needed; refresh_token is NULL because a social session has no refresh grant and re-auth is a full recapture.

nodes.label: TRD core API routes (/api/v1/*)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)

nodes.label: TRD security & cryptographic standard (AES-256-GCM)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: Unique IV per record, a 32-byte hex master key from env, and meta_data left plaintext so metadata stays queryable.

nodes.label: TRD SQLite data schema (users, credentials, agents)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: trd sqlite data schema (users, credentials, agents)
nodes.rationale: credentials is polymorphic with encrypted access/refresh tokens, a per-record iv, indexed expires_at and plaintext meta_data JSON for uninhibited metadata queries. The specified CHECK(type IN ('api_key','ray')) was never built.

nodes.label: TRD development sub-tasks (Tasks 1-4)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)

nodes.label: TRD system architecture (Bun, Next.js, Hono, SQLite, host binaries)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: trd system architecture (bun, next.js, hono, sqlite, host binaries)

nodes.label: additional_data reduced to a derived `stale` boolean
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: additional_data reduced to a derived `stale` boolean
nodes.rationale: MASKED_COLUMNS selects additional_data but toMasked drops the object and exposes only `stale`, so anything added there later stays off the wire by default rather than by someone remembering to omit it.

nodes.label: Security rule: encrypted tokens, plaintext meta_data, never logged
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: security rule: encrypted tokens, plaintext meta_data, never logged
nodes.rationale: access_token/refresh_token are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a unique IV per record while meta_data stays plaintext JSON for queryability; tokens, keys and request bodies are never logged.

nodes.label: §3.2 expires_at is a floor on uselessness
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: §3.2 expires_at is a floor on uselessness
nodes.rationale: A session can be revoked server-side long before cookie expiry, so past-expiry means definitely dead (cheap, indexed) while future means only maybe alive -- the UI must render 'Connected as @handle' and never 'valid until X'.

nodes.label: §4.4 Capture logging allowlist
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: Only source, credential_id, cookie_count, rotated and session_state are permitted; the middleware logs both request and response bodies, so capture routes must never put jar material in either and /finish returns the masked credential only.

nodes.label: §3.3 What must never enter meta_data
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: meta_data is plaintext on disk AND returned by the API, so no cookie value ever, not even a truncated prefix; cookie NAMES are fine and help diagnose a partial capture without decrypting. isSensitiveKey matching 'cookie' auto-redacts cookie_names if meta_data is ever logged -- defence in depth, not the primary control.

nodes.label: §3.5 Migration: NONE (Drizzle enum is TypeScript-level)
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: The generated DDL is plain TEXT with no CHECK constraint, so adding 'cookie' changes types only; the proof step is that db:generate must produce no new migration file. Note the TRD's CHECK(type IN ('api_key','ray')) was never built -- the code has always used api_key/oauth and the schema is the truth.

nodes.label: §3.4 Reconnect works with no new code
nodes.community_name: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.norm_label: §3.4 reconnect works with no new code
nodes.rationale: createCredential already replaces on (userId, provider, account_id) for non-api_key types, so reconnecting the same account updates in place and a second account creates a second row -- the desired behaviour inherited free.

nodes.label: Project layout (src/app, lib/db, observability, crypto, schemas)
nodes.norm_label: project layout (src/app, lib/db, observability, crypto, schemas)

nodes.label: Relay stack table (Bun, Next.js, Hono, Drizzle, Zod, Biome)
nodes.norm_label: relay stack table (bun, next.js, hono, drizzle, zod, biome)

nodes.label: §7 Phased build plan (Phases 0-6)
nodes.rationale: Each phase is independently shippable and revertible; Phase 6 is last because it is the only phase that REMOVES a working code path, and phases 1-5 are purely additive since withSourceCookies yields null with no credential stored.

nodes.label: Google Search Console site-verification file
nodes.rationale: Empty placeholder file served from the site root; its filename is the verification token.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules (read node_modules docs first)
nodes.norm_label: next.js agent rules (read node_modules docs first)
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so the agent must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code.

nodes.label: Stage completion derived from recorded timings
nodes.norm_label: stage completion derived from recorded timings
nodes.rationale: Ticks come from evidence (recorded timings), not list position, otherwise a finished run showed green on stages that do not exist yet. This is also why extract_ms collided: ingest's ffmpeg key was renamed audio_extract_ms so it could not falsely complete the agent stage. run-status.ts holds the vocabulary with only a type import so client components never pull Drizzle into the bundle.

nodes.label: The stale-worker trap
nodes.rationale: pkill -f does not kill bun on Windows because it cannot read Windows command lines, so an old worker keeps claiming jobs and running old code -- the symptom is a correct-looking failure with the OLD wording. Restart the worker after any pipeline change; kill via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process.

nodes.label: Circuit breakers (3 files/step, typecheck gate, stop for approval)
nodes.norm_label: circuit breakers (3 files/step, typecheck gate, stop for approval)
nodes.rationale: Bounded steps with a human gate: max 3 files per step, zero typecheck errors before claiming completion, update LLM_STATE.md and STOP, never commit without approval, no ghost dependencies.

nodes.label: Code hygiene: 250-line cap and backend naming
nodes.norm_label: code hygiene: 250-line cap and backend naming
nodes.rationale: Split modules before 250 lines; there is exactly ONE Hono app and everything under src/server/ is a module, never a sub-router named app.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable sequencing: consolidation lands last
nodes.rationale: Deleting the fallback downloader in the same change that introduces cookies makes a cookie bug and a consolidation bug indistinguishable; the stale-worker episode showed how expensive a correct-looking failure with old wording is.

nodes.label: Brand Palette: Emerald Green + Navy Accent on White
nodes.norm_label: brand palette: emerald green + navy accent on white

nodes.label: Agent sprawl: the router was the cause
nodes.norm_label: agent sprawl: the router was the cause
nodes.rationale: The router prompt said to choose 0 whenever unsure, so every unsure synthesized a new agent -- sensible with 2 System agents, corrosive as the library grows. The router now matches on CATEGORY not subject. resetPrompt() was needed because seedPrompts skips edited rows, freezing an edited prompt forever. Measuring first showed the taxonomy constraint and synthesis cap were unnecessary complexity.

nodes.label: disposition(): 5xx is next-model, not fail
nodes.rationale: An unnamed status fell through to fail, so one transient 503 on the top candidate ended a run with three usable models queued behind it. >=500 is now next-model, not next-provider: a busy model is not a busy provider. Likewise any LlmError with status < 400 (an empty 200 completion) is a MODEL problem, and 402 needed ChatProvider.billing because on Ollama Cloud it is per-model, not account-wide.

nodes.label: Gemini wired for extraction
nodes.rationale: Gemini had a vault key but no ChatProvider entry, so it never appeared in the order list. Added on the OpenAI-compatible surface with a capabilities fallback (its rows publish no context, features or created, so structured would be false and json_schema never sent), and placed after the MEASURED ~5s Groq rather than displacing it.

nodes.label: The gemma `excludes` wrong turn
nodes.rationale: A provider-level excludes regex dropped gemma-* on evidence that was a harness bug: the harness passed an already-wrapped schema, which double-wrapped into a schema with no type, and gemma was describing it accurately. Lesson: when a model claims the request was malformed, check the request before blaming the model.

nodes.label: isolate() and the unterminated trailing fence
nodes.norm_label: isolate() and the unterminated trailing fence
nodes.rationale: Short-circuiting on body.startsWith('{') returned the body verbatim, so a valid object followed by a bare closing fence failed to parse; it now always slices first { to last }.

nodes.label: Capability-driven model ranking heuristics
nodes.rationale: Model ids are never hardcoded: catalogs are discovered from each provider's /models, ranked on advertised capability and cached in the DB. Two documented heuristics: an id regex excluding guard/embed/tts/moderation models (a safeguard model advertises identical capabilities), and a parameter count parsed from the id, because a created-desc tiebreak picked 20b over 120b and 20b failed schema validation twice. Unknown size scores as mid-sized so declared-large > unknown > declared-small, and context is capped before ranking.

nodes.label: Ollama local + cloud provider
nodes.rationale: Both modes are OpenAI-compatible so cloud needed no special client; local is keyless and OFF by default because a keyless provider would look configured in production and burn an attempt per run. Ollama's /v1/models advertises nothing, so ChatProvider.capabilities fills it in -- the real loss without it is structured:false silently dropping schema-constrained decoding. OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is a server setting, not the model max.

nodes.label: Every prompt lives in the database with Redis hot cache
nodes.norm_label: every prompt lives in the database with redis hot cache
nodes.rationale: Prompts and the model catalog are per-user DB rows invalidated on write; the cache uses its OWN ioredis connection because BullMQ's sets enableOfflineQueue:false and a pre-handshake command throws, a trade that is backwards for a cache.

nodes.label: Provider ordering UI and user_settings
nodes.rationale: resolveExtractionOrder reconciles a saved order against the code's list (unknown ids dropped, new providers appended) so a stale preference can never stop extraction, and getExtractionOrder narrows to providers the user can actually use. Move up/down buttons are not decoration: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative to any drag.

nodes.label: versionScore(id) model ranking tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: With no size in the id and no created to sort on, id.localeCompare put retired gemini-2.5-* and non-chat models ahead of live ones, so all four MAX_CANDIDATES were garbage. versionScore sits below created (real dates are the better recency signal) and above localeCompare, rejects dates and sizes, and takes the first version token as the family version; ranking for Groq/OpenRouter/Ollama diffed IDENTICAL.

nodes.label: §4.2 withSourceCookies (materialize and destroy)
nodes.rationale: No credential yields null and the downloader omits --cookies entirely, byte-for-byte today's anonymous path -- which is what makes every phase independently shippable and instantly revertible. The jar is written chmod 600 inside the run's temp dir and deleted in a finally, with purge() as a second line of defence against a hard kill.

nodes.label: Per-credential jar lock (correctness)
nodes.rationale: Two runs sharing one cookie jar both write the rotated jar back on exit and the loser can invalidate a live session, so a cookie-bearing run takes a second lock keyed on the credential; the guarantee then holds at any concurrency instead of depending on someone remembering to re-key. Its refusal reason jar_busy is deliberately distinct from user_busy.

nodes.label: Jar write-back on a FAILED download (bug)
nodes.norm_label: jar write-back on a failed download (bug)
nodes.rationale: persistRotation ran in a finally, so a failed run overwrote the stored credential with the anonymous cookie set that failing request received. Write-back is now gated on success; whether a REAL session cookie survives yt-dlp's rewrite is still unmeasured, and if it does not, rotation is destructive rather than a freshness feature.

nodes.label: §3.6 getSecretByType (vault widening)
nodes.rationale: getAccessToken filters only on (userId, provider) with no type filter or ordering, which becomes ambiguous the moment two credential types share a provider id; a sibling function is added rather than changing the signature, returning credentialId so the reject counter can be written back.

nodes.label: §4.2 Jar rotation write-back (--cookies is read-write)
nodes.rationale: yt-dlp dumps the refreshed jar back on exit, so reading it back and re-encrypting when changed is how a session stays alive for weeks instead of expiring on its original cookie lifetime; never log the diff, only rotated: true.

nodes.label: §4.2b YouTube's stricter cookie rules
nodes.rationale: Reopening a YouTube session in a browser rotates the refresh token and invalidates the exported jar, so the capture profile dir must be single-use by explicit invariant and the registry needs a per-provider settleUrl visited immediately before harvest. Concurrent use of one jar forks the rotation chain, and using a real account carries documented ban risk that the Connect dialog must state plainly.

nodes.label: bun run verify:ytdlp acceptance test
nodes.rationale: Reproduces the client matrix with a REAL media fetch per fixture rather than --simulate, which would pass while every real run 403s; it is the gate for bumping the yt-dlp pin, triggered by yt-dlp's own >90-days-old warning.

nodes.label: Phase 0: YouTube GVS 403 and player_client fallbacks
nodes.norm_label: phase 0: youtube gvs 403 and player_client fallbacks
nodes.rationale: The recorded bot check decayed; the live failure is HTTP 403 on the media fetch after metadata resolves. The default client chain fails 3 of 6 sampled videos and download.ts passed no --extractor-args; 403 also matched no UNAVAILABLE pattern so BullMQ retried a deterministic failure. Fix is a config-driven ytDlpFallbacks chain keyed by source id, with a surviving 403 classified permanent.

nodes.label: §1.1b PO tokens rejected
nodes.rationale: The provider's own docs say PO tokens do not guarantee bypassing 403s or bot checks, and bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider needs Node.js >=20 or Deno, colliding with the Bun-first rule at the moment Branch A is trying to remove Python. Kept as a documented escalation only.

nodes.label: §1.1 YouTube GVS 403 (settled by measurement)
nodes.rationale: Metadata always resolves and only the media fetch 403s; the default client loses 3 of 6 videos while web_embedded wins 4 of 4. Cookies would not have fixed it because a GVS 403 is a SABR/PO-token-tier refusal, not an auth challenge. The list of working clients is a moving target set by YouTube, which is why it belongs in config and not a source file.

nodes.label: Risk #8: the yt-dlp pin is stale with no bump cadence
nodes.norm_label: risk #8: the yt-dlp pin is stale with no bump cadence
nodes.rationale: A hard pin gives reproducible extraction across deploys, but YouTube breaks extractors continuously, so a pin with no cadence is a slow-motion outage; the answer is a monthly bump with the client matrix as the acceptance test, never a floating tag, which trades a predictable problem for an unpredictable one.
